messages:
neil: Kicked off a 2% canary for encoder-fusion + postprocess-offload. Objective: reduce CPU/token prep and shorten end-to-end latency for mixed chat workloads.
tara: Ran a 48h replay on cluster B. Highlights: median down ~10%, p95 down ~17%, p99 down ~23%. CPU sys-time per request dropped ~28%. Token cost estimate -12%.
deploy-bot: Canary artifact: https://internal.redwood/bench/2625009876. Aggregate metrics:
```
- baseline p50 30ms -> canary p50 27ms
- baseline p95 150ms -> canary p95 125ms
- baseline p99 480ms -> canary p99 370ms
- cpu sys/request: 9.8ms -> 7.1ms
- cost/1k tokens: $0.085 -> $0.075
- 5xx rate: 0.07% -> 0.08% (no alert)
```
sven: Nice work. Any memory pressure on the host or increase in tail GC pauses from offload?
tara: No GC tail increases observed. Host mem ~+12MB average (within cushion). We added a safety fallback that routes heavy-tokenization paths to the baseline codepath.
anya: What are our canary rollback thresholds? Need them for the rollout doc and PD playbook.
neil: Config we used: 
```
canary_pct: 2
ramp: 2 -> 20 over 40m -> 100 over 3h
eval_window: 10m
rollback_triggers:
  p99_rel_increase_pct: 10
  error_rate_rel_increase_pct: 0.5
  host_mem_growth_mb: 60
  cpu_sys_increase_pct: 30
```
anya: Thanks. Product asked for a one-line blurb for the weekly note. Can you give a tight sentence + stat?
sven: Draft: "Runtime encoder-fusion + offload reduced median latency by ~10% and p99 by ~23% for mixed-chat flows; estimated token cost down ~12%."
tara: I'll attach a seq-length vs kernel heatmap to the canary artifact and a brief note describing the fallback logic. Monitoring hooks bound to runtime.encoder.*, runtime.postproc.* and host.mem.delta. PagerDuty on for 90m.
neil: If no triggers hit by 90m we ramp to 20% and continue to full. Thanks team — impressive gains for a small change. :rocket:
